title: Runecast is in Steam Next Fest — making the choices before an auto-battle readable
author: dotsmithjogos
selftext:
We're Dotsmith, a small independent studio from Brazil. Our rune-building roguelite Runecast is taking part in Steam Next Fest (October 19–26), with a free demo.



You cast runes to summon heroes, arrange your company across three lanes, and change the contents of your rune bag at the Forge. Combat plays out automatically, so the decisions you make beforehand need to be understandable.



We use generative AI as an assistant in development, with our team directing and reviewing the work. For this demo update, the practical focus has been animation, interface and battle feedback, alongside fixes from player reports. A polished image on its own doesn't tell a player why their preparation mattered; the same visual choices have to work inside a moving, information-heavy game screen. That's the part we'd like to discuss with other developers here.



When you build an auto-battler or another preparation-heavy game, how do you check that players understand what their last decision changed? Do you rely more on the preparation screen, feedback during the action, or a recap afterward?



If you'd like to see our current approach, the demo is free on Steam:

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5181900/Runecast\_Demo/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5181900/Runecast_Demo/)
